content.title: Heat vs. Cavaliers: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/25/26)
content.text: The Miami Heat (38–34) face the Cleveland Cavaliers (45–27) tonight at Rocket Arena in Cleveland. Miami enters in urgent need of a win, having dropped five straight during a difficult stretch of its schedule following a six-game winning streak. The Heat have fallen to several playoff-caliber opponents, including the Charlotte Hornets, Los Angeles Lakers, Houston Rockets, and, most recently, the San Antonio Spurs, who handed them a 136–111 defeat on Monday night. In that loss, Norman Powell led Miami with 21 points on 7-of-18 shooting, reflecting the team’s broader offensive struggles as the Heat shot just 40% from the field. Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro added 18 points apiece, but Miami had difficulty containing San Antonio’s balanced attack. Victor Wembanyama paced the Spurs with 26 points, while Keldon Johnson and Dylan Harper each contributed 21. The Heat enter tonight in 10th place in the Eastern Conference. They are tied in the standings with the Orlando Magic and the Hornets, separated only by tiebreakers. Miami sits just two games out of the final automatic playoff spot but remains positioned, at minimum, for a play-in tournament berth. Cleveland, meanwhile, arrives in strong form with four consecutive victories and currently holds fourth place in the East. The Cavaliers are 2.5 games behind the second-place team, with the top seed appearing largely out of reach at this stage. But they maintain a comfortable 4.5-game cushion over the fifth-place Toronto Raptors, making a top-four finish increasingly likely with 10 games remaining in the regular season. The Cavaliers defeated the Magic 136–131 last night behind a dominant performance from Donovan Mitchell, who poured in 42 points. James Harden added 26, while Evan Mobley finished with 19. Cleveland shot a blistering 60% from the field and 40% from three-point range, underscoring how dangerous the team can be when its primary scorers find their rhythm. Expect a tight matchup that will ultimately be determined by the efficiency of Miami’s backcourt. Cleveland has the edge here as the Heat have struggled against the league’s top teams lately. Final Score Prediction: Cleveland Cavaliers 121, Miami Heat 114 Injury Report Miami Heat Jahmir Young — GTD (Undisclosed) Terry Rozier — Out (Not injury related) Cleveland Cavaliers Max Strus — Out (Foot) Larry Nance Jr. — GTD (Illness) Jarrett Allen — Out (Knee) Jaylon Tyson — Out (Toe) Craig Porter Jr. — Out (Groin) How to Watch Heat vs. Cavaliers Tip-off for tonight’s Heat-Cavaliers game is set for 7:00 PM Eastern at Rocket Arena in Cleveland.
